tb21_profile.skill: Load a HuggingFace dataset, read its README to resolve which column/subset 'deepseek' and 'science domain' mean, tokenize with a named HF tokenizer, emit one exact integer
tb21_profile.domain: HuggingFace datasets/transformers, LLM data curation and tokenizer accounting, Python data analysis
tb21_profile.task_form: compute-an-exact-answer: measurement/aggregation over a remote dataset, single integer written to a file

verifier_notes: Terminal-Lego task_13146 (HuggingFace TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM) is graded FREE and its 12 tests really are file-exists/substring checks; kept in per_source only as the corpus's sole HF-transformers item. tw_259453 and tw_97603 also genuinely FREE (output-shape checks on a summary file), so both stay out of final_top10. CalibForge model-training_* tokenizer-count tasks graded 'ok' pin the integer answer in at least one test, which is the test that matters here; grade understates them.

notes: CalibForge is overwhelmingly the best pool here - it contains what are effectively siblings of this exact TB2.1 task (HF dataset + Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct tokenizer + integer to /app/answer.txt), which no v1 corpus has. The v1 pool's closest offerings (TMax tiktoken/HF-tokenizer pipelines) are a clear step down, and TerminalWorld/RTS/SWE-* only contribute generic dataset-counting or tokenizer-library debugging. Terminal-Lego is weak for this task: its NLP content is sklearn/Keras 'demonstrate the API' exercises with no exact-answer discipline, and its single HuggingFace item (task_13146) is FREE. Recursive-Task-Synthesis has no real defensible top-10; its Zipf word-frequency family is the honest best and several entries there are near-duplicates of each other, so the merge step should expect low diversity from that block. No FREE candidate is in final_top10.
